# Hexadecimal

Bytes as hexadecimal digits in either case, and a view that prints them.

<h2 id="hex-case"><code>HexCase</code></h2>

```rux
pub enum HexCase {
    Lower,
    Upper
}
```

Which case hexadecimal digits above nine are written in.
Copy, carrying no payload. Decoding accepts both regardless.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Encoding/Src/Hex.rux#L15)

**Cases**

| Name    | Description                                                                          |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Lower` | `a` through `f`, the form most text formats and every cryptographic test vector use. |
| `Upper` | `A` through `F`, the form RFC 4648 prints its alphabet in.                           |

<h2 id="hex-encoded-length"><code>HexEncodedLength</code></h2>

```rux
pub func HexEncodedLength(length: uint) -> uint
```

How many characters the hexadecimal form of `length` bytes occupies: exactly twice as many.
Cannot fail for any length a slice in memory can have. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Encoding/Src/Hex.rux#L27)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type   | Description                   |
| -------- | ------ | ----------------------------- |
| `length` | `uint` | the number of bytes to encode |

**Returns**: the number of characters [`HexEncode`](/docs/api/encoding/hex#hex-encode) writes

<h2 id="hex-encode"><code>HexEncode</code></h2>

```rux
pub func HexEncode(
    bytes: byte[..],
    into: var char8[..],
    letterCase: HexCase
) -> uint ! FormatError

pub func HexEncode(
    text: char8[..],
    into: var char8[..],
    letterCase: HexCase
) -> uint ! FormatError
```

Writes `bytes` as hexadecimal digits into `into`, two per byte, high nibble first.
Runs in time that depends only on the length of `bytes`. Reports `InsufficientCapacity` when `into` is shorter
than `HexEncodedLength(bytes.length)`, leaving it exactly as it was; room past the encoded form is not touched.

| Overload                                                                                              | Summary                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func HexEncode(bytes: byte[..], into: var char8[..], letterCase: HexCase) -> uint ! FormatError` | Writes `bytes` as hexadecimal digits into `into`, two per byte, high nibble first. |
| `pub func HexEncode(text: char8[..], into: var char8[..], letterCase: HexCase) -> uint ! FormatError` | Writes the bytes of `text` as hexadecimal digits into `into`, two per byte.        |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Encoding/Src/Hex.rux#L39)

**Parameters**

| Name         | Type            | Description                                                           |
| ------------ | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bytes`      | `byte[..]`      | the bytes to encode                                                   |
| `into`       | `var char8[..]` | the destination, at least `HexEncodedLength(bytes.length)` characters |
| `letterCase` | `HexCase`       | which case the digits above nine are written in                       |
| `text`       | `char8[..]`     | the text whose bytes to encode                                        |

**Returns**: the number of characters written

<h2 id="hex-decoded-length"><code>HexDecodedLength</code></h2>

```rux
pub func HexDecodedLength(text: char8[..]) -> uint ! DecodeError
```

How many bytes the hexadecimal text decodes to, after checking that its length is even.
Only the length is checked; the digits themselves are checked by [`HexDecode`](/docs/api/encoding/hex#hex-decode). Reports `InvalidLength` at the
end of the text when it has an odd number of characters. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Encoding/Src/Hex.rux#L71)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type        | Description          |
| ------ | ----------- | -------------------- |
| `text` | `char8[..]` | the hexadecimal text |

**Returns**: the number of bytes [`HexDecode`](/docs/api/encoding/hex#hex-decode) writes for it

<h2 id="hex-decode"><code>HexDecode</code></h2>

```rux
pub func HexDecode(
    text: char8[..],
    into: var byte[..]
) -> uint ! DecodeError
```

Reads hexadecimal digits of either case from `text` into `into`, one byte per pair.
Runs in time that depends only on the length of `text` when the text is valid. Reports `InvalidLength` for an
odd number of characters and `InvalidCharacter` at the first character that is not a hexadecimal digit, leaving
`into` untouched in both cases, because the whole text is checked before anything is written. Reports
`InsufficientCapacity` with the length needed when `into` is too short, also leaving it untouched.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Encoding/Src/Hex.rux#L85)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type           | Description                                              |
| ------ | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text` | `char8[..]`    | the hexadecimal text to decode                           |
| `into` | `var byte[..]` | the destination, at least `HexDecodedLength(text)` bytes |

**Returns**: the number of bytes written

<h2 id="hex-view"><code>HexView</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct HexView {
    // private fields
}
```

A borrowed byte sequence that renders as hexadecimal under a format placeholder.
Lets a caller write `Render("{}", ViewHex(digest))` instead of sizing a buffer first. The view borrows the bytes
and must not outlive them. Copy, owning nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Encoding/Src/Hex.rux#L124)

**Implements Display**

`HexView` conforms to `Display`.

<h3 id="hex-view-write-display"><code>WriteDisplay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDisplay(
    self: &HexView,
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes the bytes as hexadecimal digits, padded to the placeholder's width.
The style `x` selects lower case and `X` upper case; with neither, the view's own case is used. The digits
are produced in blocks, so rendering allocates nothing however long the bytes are. Reports whatever the writer
reported, and `UnsupportedRequest` for a precision or any other style.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole rendering was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Encoding/Src/Hex.rux#L148)

<h2 id="view-hex"><code>ViewHex</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ViewHex(
    bytes: byte[..],
    letterCase: HexCase
) -> HexView
```

Borrows `bytes` for rendering as hexadecimal.
Cannot fail and allocates nothing; the view reads `bytes` each time it is rendered, so it must not outlive them.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Encoding/Src/Hex.rux#L135)

**Parameters**

| Name         | Type       | Description                                          |
| ------------ | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `bytes`      | `byte[..]` | the bytes to render                                  |
| `letterCase` | `HexCase`  | the case used when the placeholder does not name one |

**Returns**: a view that renders `bytes` as hexadecimal
